domain_label: Flavor Pairing & Taste Balance (cupcake Flavor Design & Sensory Balance subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors grounded in canonical references
subdomain scope is flavor pairing and five-taste balance, finer than a whole cupcake-craft KB
a viable base cupcake formula and bake process already exist; structural baking chemistry is referenced not optimized here
evaluation is blind sensory tasting centric unless a project overrides the balance target
exclusions: structural baking chemistry (flour protein, leavening pH, soda:acid browning)
mixing method and gluten development beyond their effect on flavor carry
frosting structural stability, piping, and decoration technique
oven engineering, pan, and bake-time optimization
costing, sourcing, and supply-chain decisions beyond flavor impact

competency_questions.question: What balance target across the five tastes plus fat and aroma does this cupcake optimize?
How is aroma treated as a balance lever alongside the five tastes?
How is total sweetness moderated across cake and frosting to avoid a cloying bite?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SWEET_MODERATION and FROSTING_PAIRING set a sweetness budget

competency_questions.question: At what level does salt enhance without reading salty?
Which acid source and level brighten the cupcake without dominating?
How is bitter depth from cocoa or coffee balanced against sweetness?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BITTER_DEPTH and CHOCOLATE_SYSTEM set bitter balance

competency_questions.question: How is fat and umami richness tuned for mouthfeel that carries aroma?
How are complementary flavors chosen using shared-aroma logic?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SHARED_AROMA_PAIR uses shared-compound and canonical pairing

competency_questions.question: How is flavor complexity restrained so each note stays legible?
How are extracts, zest, and spices dosed for post-bake aroma?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EXTRACT_DOSING, ZEST_INFUSION, and SPICE_BLOOM set dosing

competency_questions.question: How are fruit, chocolate, and inclusions integrated for flavor without ruining texture?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FRUIT_SYSTEM, CHOCOLATE_SYSTEM, and INCLUSION_TEXTURE_FLAVOR address integration

competency_questions.question: How does vanilla round and tie the flavor set together?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VANILLA_ROUNDING and AROMA_LAYERING define the rounding/layering role

competency_questions.question: How is the assembled cake-plus-frosting bite validated for balance?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FROSTING_PAIRING and BALANCE_TASTING validate the bite

competency_questions.question: What safety and shelf-life limits override flavor choices?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FOOD_SAFETY_GATE and SHELF_FLAVOR set overriding limits

glossary.definition: the intended position across the five tastes plus fat and aroma that all dosing optimizes toward
selecting flavors that share volatile compounds because they tend to harmonize
a background flavor like vanilla that smooths edges and binds a flavor set without leading
releasing fat-soluble aroma by warming spice or cocoa in fat or hot liquid
the temporal layering of volatile aromatics from fleeting to lingering
an ingredient like salt that lifts other tastes without being perceived itself
the lifting, fresh, contrast effect of acidity against sweetness
the combined perceived sweetness of cake plus frosting eaten together
the temperature range where pathogens grow rapidly, bounding safe holding time

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for cupcake flavor-pairing and taste-balance work units, grounded in canonical references (Segnit Flavor Thesaurus; McGee On Food and Cooking; Parks BraveTart; CIA Baking and Pastry) without supplied measured datasets

nodes.definition: Map the target cupcake across the five tastes plus fat and aroma so every later dosing decision optimizes one shared balance target.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: flavor brief or reference recipe revised

pros.claim: anchors all dosing to one balance target
pros.example: sweet/salt/acid set against a single brief

cons.claim: a wrong target silently biases every later choice
cons.example: under-set sweetness target makes whole batch cloying

failure_modes: ignoring aroma as a balance lever
acceptance_tests: balance target documented across all five tastes plus fat and aroma
each later node cites this target

nodes.definition: Set total sugar to the lowest level that still reads as a dessert so other flavors are not buried, accounting for sugar's structural role.

pros.claim: lower sugar lets complexity show
pros.example: 20% sugar cut reveals citrus and spice

cons.claim: sugar also gives moisture and structure, so cuts can dry crumb
cons.example: too-low sugar yields tough, pale cake

failure_modes: cutting sugar so far texture fails
leaving sugar so high flavors flatten
acceptance_tests: sugar at or below level where added flavors are still perceptible
crumb still tender at chosen level

nodes.definition: Dose salt to suppress bitterness and lift sweetness/aroma perception without the product reading salty.

excluded: flaky finishing salt as garnish only

pros.claim: a small salt bump makes chocolate and caramel read deeper
pros.example: pinch of salt lifts caramel aroma

cons.claim: overshoot makes the cake taste savory
cons.example: heavy salt reads as bread not dessert

acceptance_tests: salt raises perceived sweetness/aroma in A/B without reading salty

nodes.definition: Add acid (citrus, buttermilk, sour cream, fruit) to brighten and contrast sweetness, choosing source by aroma fit.

excluded: acid's role in chemical leavening pH

pros.claim: acid cuts cloying sweetness and adds lift
pros.example: buttermilk brightens a vanilla crumb

cons.claim: too much acid curdles dairy and tastes sharp
cons.example: excess lemon makes batter break and pucker

acceptance_tests: acid raises perceived freshness without sourness dominating

nodes.definition: Use cocoa, dark chocolate, or coffee to add bitter depth and complexity, balancing against sweetness and salt.

pros.claim: a touch of espresso deepens chocolate without tasting of coffee
pros.example: instant espresso amplifies cocoa

cons.claim: too much cocoa/coffee turns harsh and astringent
cons.example: overdosed cocoa reads chalky and bitter

acceptance_tests: bitter source adds perceived depth without harsh astringency

nodes.definition: Tune butter/oil and dairy fat plus subtle umami (browned butter, malt) for richness and mouthfeel that carries aroma.

included: fat type and level for richness

pros.claim: browned butter adds nutty umami depth
pros.example: beurre noisette in a vanilla cupcake

cons.claim: excess fat greases mouthfeel and dulls aroma release
cons.example: oversaturated fat coats palate

acceptance_tests: fat level gives clean rich mouthfeel that carries aroma

nodes.definition: Select complementary flavors using shared-aromatic logic (foods sharing volatile compounds tend to pair) anchored to canonical pairings.

pros.claim: shared-compound pairs feel coherent
pros.example: strawberry+vanilla share vanillin-adjacent notes

cons.claim: shared-compound logic is heuristic, not guaranteed
cons.example: compound overlap can still taste odd

acceptance_tests: each pairing justified by shared aroma or canonical reference and confirmed by taste

nodes.definition: Dose extracts (vanilla, almond, citrus oils) by potency and bake-off loss so the finished cupcake hits target aroma, not the raw batter.

pros.claim: dosing for bake loss keeps aroma in the finished cake
pros.example: extra almond extract survives the oven

cons.claim: almond/citrus oils overpower fast at small overdose
cons.example: a few drops too much almond reads medicinal

acceptance_tests: target aroma present in cooled cupcake, not just batter
no artificial off-note

nodes.definition: Use citrus zest (rubbed into sugar) for fresh top-note brightness, controlling pith bitterness and oil release.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: tasting panel or recipe revision changes target balance

pros.claim: rubbing zest into sugar releases oils for vivid top notes
pros.example: lemon-sugar perfumes the whole batter

cons.claim: too much pith adds bitterness
cons.example: over-zesting into white pith turns bitter

acceptance_tests: zest gives fresh citrus top note without pith bitterness

nodes.definition: Dose and bloom spices (cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, nutmeg) in fat for warmth without dustiness or numbing overdose.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: tasting panel or recipe revision changes target balance

pros.claim: blooming spice in melted butter deepens warm aroma
pros.example: cardamom bloomed in butter reads rounder

cons.claim: overdose turns dusty, soapy, or numbing
cons.example: too much cinnamon dries the palate and dominates

acceptance_tests: spice gives warm aroma without dustiness or numbing overdose

nodes.definition: Integrate fruit (puree, freeze-dried powder, jam) for flavor and acidity while managing moisture and color without sinking or sogginess.

pros.claim: freeze-dried fruit powder concentrates flavor without added water
pros.example: freeze-dried raspberry keeps crumb dry

cons.claim: wet purees add water that weakens crumb and dilutes flavor
cons.example: fresh berries sink and weep

acceptance_tests: fruit flavor clear with crumb intact and fruit evenly distributed

nodes.definition: Engineer chocolate flavor via cocoa percentage, natural vs Dutch cocoa, and bloom-in-liquid choices to balance bitterness, acidity, and depth.

excluded: soda:acid pH leavening interaction (out of subdomain)

pros.claim: blooming cocoa in hot coffee/water amplifies chocolate aroma
pros.example: hot-water bloom deepens chocolate

cons.claim: Dutched vs natural cocoa shifts acidity and flavor unexpectedly
cons.example: wrong cocoa type flattens or sours

acceptance_tests: chocolate reads deep and balanced across bitter and acid

nodes.definition: Use vanilla as a background rounding agent that smooths edges and ties flavors together rather than as a foreground note.

included: bean vs extract vs paste choice

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: tasting panel or recipe revision changes target balance

pros.claim: vanilla rounds sharp edges and binds a flavor set
pros.example: vanilla smooths a citrus-spice cupcake

cons.claim: too much vanilla becomes a foreground note and muddies pairings
cons.example: heavy vanilla masks delicate fruit

acceptance_tests: vanilla improves cohesion without becoming the headline flavor

nodes.definition: Layer aromatics into top (zest/extract), mid (spice/fruit), and base (vanilla/cocoa/browned fat) notes for a coherent flavor arc.

pros.claim: a top/mid/base arc reads as evolving flavor
pros.example: bright zest into warm spice into vanilla base

cons.claim: crowding too many notes muddies the arc
cons.example: five competing aromatics blur together

acceptance_tests: finished cupcake shows distinct top, mid, and base notes in tasting

nodes.definition: Pair and balance frosting flavor and sweetness against the cake so the assembled bite is balanced, not doubly sweet.

pros.claim: a tangy or less-sweet frosting balances a sweet cake
pros.example: cream-cheese frosting cuts a sweet carrot cake

cons.claim: two sweet components stack into cloying overload
cons.example: sugar frosting on sweet cake is one-note

acceptance_tests: assembled cake-plus-frosting bite reads balanced, not doubly sweet

nodes.definition: Run iterative blind tastings of the assembled cupcake and adjust salt/acid/sweet/aroma to converge on the balance target.

pros.claim: blind tasting prevents developer bias from locking a flaw
pros.example: panel catches over-salting the developer missed

cons.claim: over-iterating chases noise and delays release
cons.example: endless tweaks on within-noise differences

acceptance_tests: assembled cupcake meets balance target in blind panel at agreed threshold

nodes.definition: Enforce food-safety limits (no raw-egg/raw-flour components, temperature danger zone, allergen control) that override any flavor or texture choice.

pros.claim: safety gate blocks unsafe flavor ideas before they ship
pros.example: raw-egg mousse filling rejected

cons.claim: safe substitutes may slightly constrain flavor
cons.example: heat-treated flour shifts raw-dough flavor

acceptance_tests: no raw-egg/raw-flour edible component present
allergens declared
cold chain documented

nodes.definition: Protect flavor and aroma over the product's intended shelf life, managing staling, aroma loss, and acid/fat off-flavors.

pros.claim: higher-bound vanilla/spice survives day-2 aroma loss
pros.example: spice dose set for day-2 not day-0

cons.claim: optimizing for shelf life can dull day-0 freshness
cons.example: over-stabilized batch tastes flat fresh

acceptance_tests: flavor meets target at end of intended shelf life

nodes.definition: Decide how many flavor components to include, restraining complexity so each note remains legible rather than crowding the palate.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: tasting panel or recipe revision changes target balance

pros.claim: editing to three legible notes beats six muddy ones
pros.example: drop weak orange to let cardamom shine

cons.claim: too much restraint reads plain or one-note
cons.example: cutting to a single note loses interest

acceptance_tests: each retained component is identifiable in blind tasting

nodes.definition: Balance flavor-carrying inclusions (chips, nuts, candied fruit) for taste contribution against texture and even distribution.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: tasting panel or recipe revision changes target balance

pros.claim: toasted nuts add flavor and contrast
pros.example: toasted pecans deepen a brown-sugar cupcake

cons.claim: heavy inclusions sink and create dense pockets
cons.example: large chips sink and weigh down crumb

acceptance_tests: inclusions evenly distributed and add flavor without dominating texture

conflict_axes.trigger: high sugar masks the paired and layered flavors
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if added notes are not perceptible, flavor complexity dominates and sugar is lowered
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: added note not identified by >40% of panel

conflict_axes.trigger: both cake and frosting carry full sweetness
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: total-bite sweetness budget dominates; the sweeter component is cut first
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: assembled bite rated cloying by panel
conflict_axes.example: sweet cake plus sugar buttercream reads one-note

conflict_axes.trigger: added moist fruit/acid weakens crumb structure
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if crumb fails, structure dominates and wet forms are replaced with concentrated ones

conflict_axes.trigger: rich tender batter resists rise and even doming
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: sensory tenderness target dominates within a safe rise window
conflict_axes.example: very rich batter sinks in the center

conflict_axes.trigger: fresh-tasting choices degrade over shelf life
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: for packaged product, shelf-life stability dominates day-0 freshness
conflict_axes.example: fresh zest gone by day two

conflict_axes.trigger: shortcut ingredients trade flavor quality for speed
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if quality gap is detectable, quality dominates for hero flavors
conflict_axes.example: imitation vanilla vs real bean paste

conflict_axes.trigger: deep bitter cocoa fights bright acidic lift
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the chosen primary character dominates; the other becomes a measured accent
conflict_axes.example: dark chocolate plus raspberry needs one to lead

conflict_axes.trigger: pushing salt for enhancement risks reading salty
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: not-salty perception dominates; back off to the threshold
conflict_axes.example: caramel cupcake tips from rounded to savory

conflict_axes.trigger: adding layers crowds the palate into mud
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: legibility dominates; cut to the notes a taster can name
conflict_axes.example: six aromatics collapse into generic spice

dominance_rules.trigger: a flavor or texture choice conflicts with food safety or allergen control
dominance_rules.rule: food safety, raw-ingredient avoidance, danger-zone limits, and allergen control override all flavor and texture choices
dominance_rules.required_action: reject unsafe component; require human review
dominance_rules.example: raw-egg mousse filling rejected despite flavor gain

dominance_rules.trigger: cake and frosting sweetness both run high
dominance_rules.rule: the assembled-bite sweetness budget dominates; cut the sweeter component
dominance_rules.required_action: reduce sugar in the higher component
dominance_rules.example: reduce buttercream sugar over a sweet cake

dominance_rules.trigger: added flavor notes are not perceptible at the chosen sugar level
dominance_rules.rule: flavor legibility dominates; lower sugar until paired notes are perceptible

dominance_rules.trigger: wet fruit or acid threatens crumb structure
dominance_rules.rule: crumb structure dominates; replace wet forms with concentrated ones
dominance_rules.required_action: switch to freeze-dried or reduced fruit

dominance_rules.trigger: product must hold flavor over shelf life
dominance_rules.rule: for packaged product, shelf-life stability dominates day-0 freshness in aroma dosing
dominance_rules.example: raise spice dose for day-2 aroma

dominance_rules.trigger: salt pushed for enhancement starts reading salty
dominance_rules.rule: not-salty perception dominates; back salt off to the enhancement threshold

dominance_rules.trigger: too many aromatics crowd the palate
dominance_rules.rule: legibility dominates; edit to the notes a taster can name

dominance_rules.trigger: blind panel and developer preference disagree
dominance_rules.rule: blind panel result dominates developer bias on balance
